proposed_comments.title: Queue snap placement outside the low-level mouse hook
proposed_comments.body:
### Queue snap placement outside the low-level mouse hook

**Severity:** `high`

The release handler performs snap work directly from the `WH_MOUSE_LL` callback, including recalculating overlay metrics and moving or maximizing an arbitrary cross-process window. If that target is busy or hung, these operations can exceed `LowLevelHooksTimeout` and Windows may silently remove GrabAndMove's mouse hook. Post a snap request to the module's message window and perform the placement there, while carrying the release-time rectangle so the final snap does not depend on the throttled preview state.
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The correction requires coordinating the button-up hook path, a queued request payload, and the message-window handler; it is not safely represented by one localized current-diff replacement.
proposed_comments.outOfDiffReason: The correction requires coordinating the button-up hook path, a queued request payload, and the message-window handler; it is not safely represented by one localized current-diff replacement.

confidence.rationale: The upstream release path visibly performs cross-process snap operations from the low-level hook, while the converged fork fix moves that sequence to the message window and preserves the release-time rectangle.

proposed_comments.title: Maximize on the selected monitor without overwriting restore bounds
proposed_comments.body:
### Maximize on the selected monitor without overwriting restore bounds

**Severity:** `high`

The maximize branch discards the `targetRect` selected from the release point and maximizes the window according to its current monitor, so a cross-monitor drag can maximize on the source monitor instead of the previewed destination. The placement sequence also needs to preserve the release-time normal rectangle and convert it to the appropriate workspace coordinates before selecting the destination monitor; otherwise restoring the maximized window can jump to a stale or taskbar-offset position. Use a two-stage placement that first selects the destination monitor and then maximizes without replacing the user's normal bounds.
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The fix spans monitor selection, WINDOWPLACEMENT normal-position preservation, tool-window coordinate handling, and the maximize operation; a single safe apply-ready range would be misleading.
proposed_comments.outOfDiffReason: The fix spans monitor selection, WINDOWPLACEMENT normal-position preservation, tool-window coordinate handling, and the maximize operation; a single safe apply-ready range would be misleading.

confidence.rationale: The current maximize path ignores the computed target rectangle, and the converged fork review added destination-monitor placement plus release-time restore-coordinate handling to address the resulting cross-monitor and restore-position failures.

proposed_comments.title: Recompute side and corner snap bounds after moving monitors
proposed_comments.body:
### Recompute side and corner snap bounds after moving monitors

**Severity:** `medium`

Side and corner snaps measure the window's invisible-frame margins before moving it to the destination monitor, then issue one asynchronous move using those source-monitor measurements. With per-monitor DPI or a `WM_DPICHANGED` response, the non-client margins can change during the transition and the visible frame can miss the previewed half or quarter. Use destination-aware, two-pass placement and recalculate the final bounds after the window reaches the target monitor.
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The correction depends on sequencing the destination move, DPI transition, margin measurement, and final placement; it cannot be reduced to one independently safe current-diff line.
proposed_comments.outOfDiffReason: The correction depends on sequencing the destination move, DPI transition, margin measurement, and final placement; it cannot be reduced to one independently safe current-diff line.

confidence.rationale: The current code measures overlay margins before the asynchronous destination move, and the converged fork review retained destination-aware two-pass placement as the fix for per-monitor-DPI behavior.

proposed_comments.title: Bound delayed focus restoration after asynchronous maximize
proposed_comments.body:
### Bound delayed focus restoration after asynchronous maximize

**Severity:** `medium`

When maximizing asynchronously, focus restoration must wait until the target is actually maximized, but the retry state needs a bounded lifetime and must be cleared when the target cannot complete. Otherwise a hung or nonconforming target can leave a timer running indefinitely, and an unconditional foreground restore can steal focus from an application the user activated while the snap was completing. Cap the retries and restore the previous foreground window only when the snap target is still the foreground window.
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The fix spans timer state, asynchronous completion detection, retry cleanup, and foreground-window validation; it is not safe as one localized suggestion.
proposed_comments.outOfDiffReason: The fix spans timer state, asynchronous completion detection, retry cleanup, and foreground-window validation; it is not safe as one localized suggestion.

confidence.rationale: The upstream asynchronous maximize path lacks the bounded focus-restoration state added by the converged fork, and the Copilot loop identified both indefinite retry and stale-focus-stealing risks.
